entities.name: Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fadrique Álvarez de Toledo y Enríquez, 2nd Duke of Alba, emerged as a preeminent military commander and statesman during a pivotal era of Spanish expansion and consolidation, spanning the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Born into the powerful House of Alba in 1460 within the Kingdom of Castile, he inherited his ducal title in 1488 and dedicated his career to serving the Catholic Monarchs, Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile, and later Emperor Charles V. His leadership was instrumental in transforming Spain into a dominant European power, particularly through his strategic brilliance and often ruthless effectiveness in warfare across the Iberian Peninsula and Italy. He embodied the martial aristocracy that underpinned the nascent Spanish Empire.

His military career began in earnest during the final phase of the Reconquista, participating in the Granada War (1482-1492) and the decisive siege of Granada. Following this, he played a crucial role in the War of the Castilian Succession and numerous campaigns to consolidate royal authority within Spain. Most notably, he led the Castilian forces that conquered the Kingdom of Navarre in 1512, integrating it definitively into the Spanish crown. His service extended to the Italian Wars, where he commanded Spanish armies against France. A highlight of his strategic acumen was his participation in the Battle of Pavia in 1525, which saw the capture of King Francis I of France and a decisive victory for Charles V's forces, cementing Spanish hegemony in Italy for decades.
